name: Balanced score of a response against its quality profile
purpose: One balanced score for each quality profile, with the weights and targets of the profile fixed before any method is scored.
record: A quality profile is a named set of criteria with weights and target values. A profile change is a new version of the metric, so scores under different profiles are never mixed. The leaderboard compares response-quality methods under each profile, the default profile first. The default profile draws on public response-quality recommendations and evaluations (see the Response Quality area of the registry). First stage: fifteen invented, neutral responses with the evidence text they are held to (evaluation/response_quality/build_cases.py), in four families (figure, dash, date, link) plus a clean one; each arm must report exactly the findings the rule of the case gives and nothing for the rules it does not judge. The weights and budgets are fixed in esoi.toml before any arm is scored.
disadvantages: Few cases, all invented to exercise one rule each, and they cover the criteria that have an arm (faithfulness to evidence, tone fit); the other criteria of the default profile are not measured. The repair of an arm is covered by its own tests, not by this score.
cascading_conditionals: free [sample=full | real=no | gate=competitive | when=the arm and its rivals were recorded on the same cases]
command: esoi run response_quality --impl evidence_check; esoi run response_quality --impl grounded_figures; esoi run response_quality --impl em_dash_free; esoi run response_quality --impl date_arithmetic
